supersedes: SourceAssets/Art/Creatures/Duck (untracked stylised candidate: SK_Duck, SK_Duck_Headless, SM_Duck_Head)
source_blend: Duck/SK_Duck.blend (three collections plus the hidden high-poly DuckHigh)
slot_note: First four keep the candidate names and share T_Duck_Atlas_*. MI_Duck_FeatherCards (masked, two-sided) uses T_Duck_FeatherCards_* for wing primaries, tail fan and a few flank feathers. Gore variants: SK_Duck_Headless and SM_Duck_Head swap MI_Duck_Feather for MI_Duck_Feather_Bloody (T_Duck_Atlas_Bloody_BC/ORM, same N) and add MI_Duck_Gore (T_Duck_Gore_*, the neck cross-section).
rig_compatibility: Existing 23-bone armature and all nine actions (Idle, Walk, Run, Peck, Quack, Hit, Death, HeadlessRun, HeadlessDeath, 30 fps) carried over untouched. Body skinned with bone heat with wing, shin, foot and jaw influences stripped from the plumage; bill, legs, feet, eyes rigid; wing shells blend wing -> wingtip. SK_Duck_Headless shares the armature (import against the SK_Duck skeleton). Verified by rendering Walk f4, Peck f18, Quack f8 and HeadlessRun f4.
importer_notes: One FBX per LOD (Export/<Asset>_LOD0..2.fbx) plus one armature-only FBX per clip, written with the same recipe as the existing creature exporters (metres source, temporary x100 export scene, FBX_SCALE_ALL, Armature wrapper node, no leaf bones). Import each LOD explicitly, as Scripts/import_creature_art.sh does. Normal maps are OpenGL (green up): keep the importer green-channel flip used by the existing creature manifests. ORM = AO/roughness/metallic, linear. SSS map (linear, single channel) is a subsurface weight mask for the creature material; without a subsurface profile the asset still reads, only flatter. SM_Duck_Head is a static prop (three LOD FBXs, no UCX hull authored; a simple sphere collision is enough). The earlier candidate was never imported, so this is a first import.

gore.note: Decapitation kept: neck bisected, wound capped with a modelled-in-texture cross-section (vertebra, cord, trachea, oesophagus, vessels, fat, skin) and blood soaking the plumage around the cut and running down the breast (texture-space composite from a baked position map).

status: NOT photoreal and NOT ready to import: an unresolved shading defect leaves black patches on the plumage (see first weakness). Reads as a white duck otherwise at gameplay distance; fails at 1 m.
known_weaknesses: BLOCKING DEFECT, unresolved: black patches on the back between the wings, in a ring under the head and on one side of the breast, in every baked review render (final_mid.png, final_back.png, final_close.png). Ruled out: bake ray misses (a position-map fill changed nothing), collapsed UV faces (none found), cage size (0.007 and 0.012 m give the same patches). Only about 10,400 texels of the 2048 atlas are black, far too few for the area affected, so the cause is probably on the mesh side (zero-length normals or inverted faces on the decimated low body or on the wing/tail cards), not in the textures. Next step: render LOD0 with a plain grey material to separate mesh from texture.
Plumage is a baked relief of about 2,000 modelled contour feathers plus wing tracts; at 1 m the feathers read as stiff overlapping scales, not soft vanes with barbs.

Contour-feather cards were built and then removed after review (they looked like stuck-on paper tabs). Only wing primaries and the tail fan are alpha cards, so the body silhouette is a smooth shell. The brief asked for contour feather cards over the base: only partly met.
Folded wings are lens-shaped shells with baked feather rows: they read as pillows from above, with a blunt trailing end.
Head plumage is an anisotropic noise bump (reads like yarn at 0.5 m); the head is close to a sphere. The bill is a clean orange spatula: nostrils and nail are modelled, lamellae are not.
White plumage clips to pure white in full sun under the review tone curve (review exposure was lowered by 0.7 stop); base colour is about 0.66-0.76 linear, check it in engine.
Feet: webs are flat two-sided sheets, toes are simple tubes with a scale bump.
Gore: blood on the plumage is a texture-space composite (soft-edged, no clotting or matting); the wound is a flat capped section with a painted cross-section, no protruding bone or trachea geometry.
Cards reuse atlas cells, so the validator reports UV overlap on LOD0, and the mesh has 5 material slots.
